data.narrative:
Enfabrica is a Series C-stage semiconductor design company that has raised $311.1M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a peer universe of eight private companies and three public semiconductor benchmarks (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) operating in the same sector.

Two quantitative methods anchor the analysis. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement to the $311M total raised proxy, yielding $529M. Peer-median triangulation across four same-sector comparables—Tenstorrent ($2.7B, Series D), Nearfield Instruments ($1.6B, Series D), Positron AI ($1.0B, Series B), and DEEPX ($529M, Series C)—produces a median valuation of $1.3B, with a range spanning $529M to $2.7B. Public-comp anchoring via price-to-sales multiples (21.4x median across the three public tickers) cannot be applied absent disclosed revenue figures, which remain unavailable for private companies.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $450M (low) to $1.5B (high), with a median point of $914M. The peer-median method pulls toward the upper end given Enfabrica's stage positioning relative to later-stage funded peers. Key uncertainties include the absence of revenue data, which would strengthen public-comp anchoring, and variation in peer maturity and market positioning within the semiconductor design segment.
